chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:
“There is no harm in the blood of fleas and bedbugs, and the urine of bats.”
Because this narration is anomalous, and it is possible that it was issued under taqiyyah.

key_terms.الرِّوَايَةَ شَاذَّةٌ: a narration regarded as anomalous or irregular
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal problem
key_terms.لِلتَّقِيَّةِ: under taqiyyah; precautionary dissimulation in context

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the impurity of flea blood, bedbug blood, and bat urine?
ai.summary: This report states that there is no problem with the blood of fleas and bedbugs and the urine of bats. The closing note indicates that the narration is considered anomalous and may have been issued under taqiyyah, which affects its legal weight in jurisprudential discussion.
